articles.headline: Sizing up NFL Week 7: Time to trust the Giants? Start Mendoza? Worry about Henry?
articles.description: Let's make sense of six takeaways from Sunday and spin them forward. Just how good is the Vikings' defense? What's wrong with the Ravens' run game? Are the Giants legit?
articles.body:
Seven weeks isn't a long time, but it might as well be an eternity in football. Seven weeks ago, we were wondering whether the Chargers might be the most explosive offense of the 2026 NFL season, if anybody would be able to stop the Rams from marching to the Super Bowl and whether the Browns were actively tanking to land Arch Manning with the first overall pick in next year's draft. A lot has changed.

Of course, in a league where each week can feel monumental and significant, actually separating the passing trends from what's really meaningful is both difficult and important. This time a year ago, the Chiefs' offensive struggles might have felt like a mirage, but they turned out to be real. And while Sam Darnold's hot start didn't stick around into the second half, the Seahawks quarterback established that he had a higher ceiling than most of us would have expected before later showing that off with a brilliant performance in the critical NFC title game victory over the Rams.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

Today, I want to take a closer look at some of the key players and storylines from Sunday's action and try to get a sense of whether what we saw was a notably good (or bad) day or a more substantial trend. And with two of the three unbeaten teams heading into Week 7 losing for the first time, it only seems reasonable to start with the last remaining undefeated.

Jump to whether it's time to:

... call the Vikings defense historically great

... give up on the Texans' defense as elite

... treat the Giants as NFC East favorites

... move on from Glenn as Jets HC

... start Mendoza in Las Vegas

... start worrying about Henry in Baltimore

Is it time to ... start treating the Vikings as a historically great defense?

I don't think anybody is too surprised that the Vikings are fielding one of the best defenses in football. Brian Flores' unit was fourth in the NFL in points allowed per drive in 2024 and then again in 2025. There were changes during the offseason, notably the departure of edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, but the Vikings brought back Flores and many of the pieces that fueled the team's success over the past couple of seasons. Projecting the Vikings to be a top-five defense heading into 2026 wouldn't have been controversial.

The Vikings are not just a top-five defense, though. They're No. 1, and it isn't particularly close. Through six games, Minnesota is allowing 1.1 points per possession. To put that in context, there's only one other team in the NFL allowing fewer than 1.7 points per drive, and that's the defending champion Seahawks at 1.4. After allowing the Packers to score two touchdowns in the first half of Week 1, Flores' defense has allowed a total of four offensive touchdowns over the ensuing five and a half games.

Is that historically great? It depends on where you set your cutoffs. Elite defenses from the turn of the century, such as the 2000 Ravens and 2002 Buccaneers, were playing in a different era of football w

articles.headline: NBA breakout players: 30 ready for the next step (yes, even Wemby and Luka)
articles.description: Steady starter to an All-Star lock? Top-10 talent to an MVP? Breakout seasons take many forms in the NBA. Ben Golliver identifies 30 players primed to take the next step.
articles.body:
Career progression can take many forms in the NBA: cracking the starting lineup, earning a first All-Star selection or making the leap into the MVP conversation, to name a few.

Let's survey which players are primed for breakout campaigns by first acknowledging that "breakout" can have very different meanings depending on a player's talent and experience.

The 30 players listed below are all primed to take the next step in 2026-27 and have been sorted into tiers based on their current credentials and the circumstances contributing to their projected improvement.

Jump to a tier:

Breakouts to: MVP | Superstar | All-Star | Starter

Breakout picks featuring: Recent trades | Rookies

Tier 1: First MVP?

Who makes the cut: Multitime All-Stars who could conceivably break through to their first MVP in 2026-27.

Victor Wembanyama, Spurs

Last season, Wembanyama finished third in MVP voting and led the Spurs to the Finals during his age-22 campaign, cementing his status as the NBA's top blue-chip prospect since LeBron James. After proving he could captain an elite defense and survive the Western Conference's playoff gauntlet, the French center must refine his isolation scoring game and become a more dependable closer to claim the "Best in the World" throne. Given his rapid improvement during his first three seasons, those developments feel like a matter of "when," not "if."

Luka Doncic, Lakers

The Lakers have fully recalibrated around the 27-year-old Doncic, who is perennially one of the league's top scorers and passers. Doncic has never finished higher than third in MVP voting, but his candidacy should benefit from a new-look supporting cast that's tailored to his strengths and an expected spike in usage after James' offseason departure. Doncic's health looms as a potential drawback: His best chance to win MVP relies on the Lakers finishing with 50-plus wins, a bar they won't clear if he misses significant time.

Cade Cunningham, Pistons

The low-key Cunningham might not generate as much buzz as some of his contemporaries, but he checks all the boxes for aspiring MVPs by putting up big numbers, driving wins and serving as the reliable face of a Finals contender. The 2021 No. 1 pick finished fifth in MVP voting last season after leading Detroit to 60 wins and the East's No. 1 seed. If the Pistons defy their preseason doubters and finish in the conference's top tier again, the 25-year-old Cunningham will almost certainly show up on more ballots this time around.

Anthony Edwards, Timberwolves

Similar to Wembanyama and Cunningham, Edwards is another former No. 1 pick on the ascent. The 25-year-old shooting guard hasn't yet finished in the top five for MVP voting, but he has led the Timberwolves on multiple deep postseason runs and is flanked by a potent new sidekick in LaMelo Ball. articles.headline: Gary Neville: Some Man United players 'aren't that professional'
articles.description: Gary Neville has launched a scathing tirade at Manchester United's players following their latest heavy defeat.
articles.body:
Gary Neville has launched a scathing tirade at Manchester United's players following their latest heavy defeat.

The former United captain and Sky Sports pundit, who watched Sunday's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford from the commentary box, said "some of them walk around like they're King William... they're not, they're nothing."

United boss Michael Carrick's job has been left hanging by a thread after his side followed up Wednesday's 4-0 Champions League humbling in Como with a sixth defeat in 12 games in all competitions this season.

Neville said on his Gary Neville podcast: "There's a few of them that aren't that professional. There's a couple of them... I live in Manchester, they're not that professional, some of them.

"I've got no time for them. There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time. Don't eat the right things. Don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every single day.

"They are not living and breathing this football club, as they should be, like professionals should.

"And why? Why? Because it's gone to their heads. But they still walk around like they're King William... they're not, they're nothing.

"Nothing, some of those players. I can't believe the... lack of standards. There was a banner in the first half that was held up in the Stretford End -- 'standards.' They went a long time ago."

- Man United are stuck with their underperforming players no matter who's manager

- Sources: United consider Howe, Nagelsmann to replace under-fire Carrick

- Gary Neville: Michael Carrick exit 'probably necessary' for Man United

Neville defended Carrick, describing his former teammate as "a brilliant man" with "integrity, credibility, decency, professionalism," laying the blame for United's Premier League slide squarely at the players.

He added: "He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno's turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes."

articles.headline: Chelsea will 'keep confidence' in Mike Penders - Xabi Alonso
articles.description: Xabi Alonso and Maxence Lacroix have thrown their support behind Mike Penders after the 21-year-old's own goal led to Saturday's 2-0 loss to Tottenham.
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso and Maxence Lacroix have thrown their support behind Mike Penders after the 21-year-old's own goal led to Saturday's 2-0 loss to Tottenham.

The Belgian goalkeeper made his first Premier League start at Stamford Bridge, where he punched the ball into his own net from a corner in the 77th minute.

Cole Palmer was then sent off for a second yellow card, and Mathys Tel wrapped up the win with an 87th-minute goal.

Blues boss Alonso, who confirmed Penders would start Wednesday's Carabao Cup fourth-round meeting at Liverpool, told the club's website: "It's part of the business; you need to deal with mistakes and we keep confidence in Mike.

"We win and we lose together and it's part of the job to deal with mistakes, myself as well as everyone.

"We support Mike and Geo [Quenda] as well, the guys starting their first [Premier League] games. He will want to prove he can do better -- and we also have to show that."

Lacroix said: "He is a young goalkeeper and he has a lot of talent. He will learn from this. This can happen in football careers and in life.

"Everyone makes mistakes, and we have to be with him and we are going to be with him. We are behind him. He will help us this season and now we have to help him."

Sunday's defeat was only the second time Chelsea have lost to Spurs at home in the Premier League era.

The Blues will travel to Anfield for the cup clash before taking on struggling Manchester United in the Premier League on Saturday.

- Dele Alli proves Spurs' good luck charm at Stamford Bridge again

- Chelsea's Xabi Alonso after Tottenham defeat: 'We lose together,' not fault of Mike Penders

- Roberto De Zerbi: Tottenham are 'a complete team' after win at Chelsea

Lacroix added: "[Liverpool] is a big game for us. We want to go far in this competition and it's good that we have a game like this now.

"We have to move on and work on some details to be stronger in certain moments and change some situations.

"We have to show the reaction of a competitor. We want to show another face, we want to win there, and it's going to be a big game."

articles.headline: Seahawks contain Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III in RB's return to Seattle
articles.description: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had his worst game of the season in his return to Seattle on Sunday night.
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III watched the final play of Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, and, unlike his teammates also on the sideline, he never approached the middle of the field to interact with the opponent.

Instead, Walker headed to the Chiefs' locker room inside Lumen Field, electing not to talk, shake hands or congratulate his former Seahawks teammates.

In his anticipated return to Seattle -- the first Super Bowl MVP to play against his former team the following season -- Walker had his worst game with the Chiefs. 

"S---, we lost," Walker said in explaining his decision. "I was frustrated. That's about it. I [saw] them over there celebrating and s---. That's about it."

Entering Sunday's primetime matchup, Walker's presence and playmaking ability -- he had a league-leading 665 rushing yards during Kansas City's 5-0 start, the most in a player's first five games with a new team in NFL history -- made him a focal point for both teams.

The Seahawks also entered Lumen Field with an impressive streak, having completed 35 consecutive games, including the playoffs, without allowing a 100-yard rusher.

In the strength-against-strength battle, Walker couldn't break many tackles or create a memorable highlight. He finished with a season-low 36 rushing yards on 14 attempts.

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes targeted Walker four times, completing each of those attempts, but Walker recorded just 21 receiving yards.

"They've got playmakers, you know," Walker said of the Seahawks' defenders. "They played hard, and they outplayed us. We've just got to get better."

Perhaps the biggest surprise for Walker and the Chiefs was that they couldn't punish the Seahawks when just seven defenders were in the box. On Walker's eight rushing attempts against seven defenders in the box, he produced just 19 yards, according to Next Gen Stats.

Before Sunday, Walker had generated seven plays in which he gained at least 20 rushing yards or more, tied with Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson for the most in the league, despite Walker playing one fewer game than Robinson. The Seahawks, who spent most of the game playing two deep safeties, never let Walker gain at least 10 yards on a single carry.

The Seahawks played nickel or dime personnel on all 50 of the Chiefs' snaps Sunday night. Entering Sunday, the Chiefs led the NFL with 7.3 yards per play against five or more defensive backs, according to Next Gen Stats.

"I ain't going to lie, I did," Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori said of wanting to limit Walker's production. "I definitely did want to hold him under 100 [yards]. I don't really listen to all the media noise, but that was my motivation. I know a lot of dudes on the defense, that was their motivation, too, to stop him under 100 and play lights out on defense. I think we did that."

articles.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 150 receiving yards, TD in Seahawks' win vs. Chiefs
articles.description: Jaxon Smith-Njigba wasn't the main story heading into Sunday night's Chiefs-Seahawks matchup -- but he emerged as the game's biggest star, continuing his own historic start by catching nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's 20-3 win.
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- Jaxon Smith-Njigba wasn't the main story heading into Sunday night's matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs, a game that marked Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III's return to Lumen Field amid his scorching start to the season.

But Smith-Njigba -- not his former teammate -- was the game's biggest star.

The NFL's leading receiver and reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year continued his historic start by catching nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's 20-3 win. Smith-Njigba has 867 receiving yards this season. That's 231 yards more than anyone else, and, according to ESPN Research, it's tied with Lance Alworth in 1965 for the eighth most through seven games in NFL history.

"He's tremendous," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. "I don't know how else to describe him. He's had some adversity this week. Just going to leave it like that. But just really proud of him as a person. As a person, competitor, teammate, how do you not just have the most respect for the guy and love him for how he operates?"

Smith-Njigba's 27-yard touchdown in the second quarter was his eighth of the season, and that also leads the NFL. The TD occurred on a play that quarterback Sam Darnold changed at the line of scrimmage before floating a pass down the left sideline to Smith-Njigba, who was being covered one-on-one by cornerback Mansoor Delane.

The Chiefs hadn't allowed a touchdown catch to an opposing receiver during their 5-0 start entering Week 7.

"I have pretty good confidence that if we're throwing him the ball, he's going to come down with it," Macdonald said. "When you see him singled like that ... I knew that's where Sam was going to go with the ball."

Of Seattle's 11 third-down conversions (in 16 chances) Sunday night, four were via Darnold throws to Smith-Njigba, including the touchdown and a 33-yard catch-and-run that was Seattle's longest play of the game.

According to ESPN Research, Smith-Njigba is the sixth player in NFL history to have six 100-yard receiving games within his team's first seven games. He's the seventh player ever and the first in the Super Bowl era (which began in 1966) with at least 850 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns in his team's first seven games.

After finishing 2025 with 1,793 receiving yards -- eighth most in NFL history -- Smith-Njigba is on pace to top Calvin Johnson's single-season record of 1,964 from 2012.

"He's unguardable," Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori said. "It's pretty amazing to see. I'm sitting there thinking like, 'Wow, this is a potential Hall of Famer.' He's a great receiver. Knowing that he's getting double-teamed and they're sending cloud his way, and he's still making plays, it's crazy. It's like, you can't even fathom it. Big ups to him. He's one of one."

articles.headline: How Payton Pritchard became Boston's unlikely iso king
articles.description: The sixth man supreme doggedly sharpens his game in brutal summer practices. That's an edge the C's will need.
articles.body:
PAYTON PRITCHARD IS at the Celtics bench when he feels a tap on his shoulder.

It's late April, and time is running out in Game 3 of the first round of the playoffs. Boston has padded its lead to 103-98 with just over a minute to go, and a win on the road in Philadelphia is in sight. That's what the Celtics usually do, after all: beat the Sixers in the playoffs, every time they've met in the postseason in the past 44 years. Pritchard has rained 3s tonight, five in all, to help with their latest effort, so who knows what kind of Philly-cooked hospitality awaits Pritchard right now.

He turns to find a man even shorter than he is -- a rarity for Pritchard on NBA courts -- who is swathed in all black. Black leather jacket, black T-shirt, black baseball cap. It all provides a stark canvas for the man's necklace, a blinged-out Roman numeral III, that glints when it hits the arena lights just right, and --

"Oh, s---," Pritchard thinks. "That's ..."

Allen Iverson looks at Pritchard, Pritchard remembers, and says: "You're the coldest white boy I've ever seen."

A CASE STUDY in being cold: Nobody in the league had a better effective field goal percentage on isolation plays than Pritchard last season (58.6%). Not Nikola Jokic (57.1%), nor Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (56.4%), nor Luka Doncic (55.8%). At the midpoint of the 2025-26 season, he was averaging 1.30 points per iso possession (minimum 100 possessions), according to Stat Defender, and had he kept up that pace, it would've been the highest mark for any player in the past decade. Pritchard trailed off in the second half of the season, but according to NBA.com, his 1.11 PPP for the season was still third highest in the league, placing him behind Doncic and SGA.

He is the NBA's unlikeliest iso king. And so it only makes sense that in the presence of Iverson, patron saint of undersized iso kings, Pritchard's most urgent thought is this: "That's AI."

And his second-most urgent thought: "I gotta turn up. Now I gotta go crazy."

The Celtics have been toying with the Sixers' emotions in the fourth quarter, letting them get close late -- down by three points, then one, then two. At which point, with a little more than a minute left, Pritchard decides to break some spirits.

"HE'S A KILLER," play-by-play man Eric Collins screams on the broadcast, fittingly, as Pritchard sinks a step-back 26-footer right as the buzzer sounds.

Pritchard saves most of his fireworks for Game 4, though, two days later. He nails a one-legged, buzzer-beating 3 at the end of the first quarter; carries Boston in the first half -- he scores 18 points to the starting five's combined 24; and finishes the night with a game and playoff career-high 32.

Pritchard does all this from the bench because that's what he is: a bench player. In fact, he's the gold standard for bench players, two seasons removed from being crowned Sixth Man of the Year. Actually, he's a starter in this league, or at least can be, like he was last season for 50 game

articles.headline: New England No.1? James Trafford tipped by Leeds boss
articles.description: Daniel Farke praised James Trafford's potential following a solid display in Leeds' 0-0 draw against Sunderland.
articles.body:
Daniel Farke praised James Trafford's potential following a solid display in Leeds' 0-0 draw against Sunderland.

The 24-year-old goalkeeper twice denied Black Cats striker Brian Brobbey in the first half and was called into action again after the break to stop Nilson Angulo.

Trafford joined Leeds from Manchester City over the summer for a reported fee of £40 million ($53m) plus bonuses and Farke was impressed with his display as the Yorkshire side secured a clean sheet.

"I wouldn't say there was an unbelievable, world class save, but several good saves and he has shown also today why we were so desperate to sign him," Farke said.

"Yes, his natural belief and skills, his aura and confidence also inspires the players in front of him but to be honest, I was expecting a performance like this from him, this is why we spent some money on him.

"I expect also a goalkeeper for Leeds on this level in a difficult away game to be the here and there. I don't expect anything less than the performance that he showed today.

"Of course, he's for me the most promising young goalkeeper in the UK and he has all potential, more or less, to be also one day England's No. 1.

"He shows this capability for us day in, week in, week out, but he has to keep going and show this with consistency. Again, I expect performances like this because he has potential to do this and nevertheless, we are all happy to have him."
